title: Critics warned about Flock surveillance. Three Houston-area investigations are fueling those concerns.

reports.title: Fort Bend County Sheriff's Office lieutenant admits to improper use of Flock cameras per docs
Critics warned about Flock surveillance. Three Houston-area investigations are fueling those concerns.

summary:
A Fort Bend County Sheriff's Office lieutenant improperly used Flock license plate cameras to look up one plate 41 times and another plate 148 times between January 2022 and December 2025. The lieutenant admitted the searches were not for official law enforcement work. A resident had filed a complaint saying the lieutenant was stalking them and that they feared for their family's safety. The lieutenant said the drivers were lurking near the lieutenant's home and family, and described a very contentious familial relationship with one vehicle owner.

An internal affairs investigation found the lieutenant violated department rules and suspended the lieutenant for two days. The lieutenant is not facing criminal charges and said the information was not shared or used. ABC13 has asked the lieutenant and the sheriff's office for comment and is waiting for a response. A law professor noted that improper access alone is usually an administrative or ethical violation unless there is clear intent to harm.
